title: New Non-Destructive Surface Roughness Inspection of Additively Manufactured Metallic Parts Using Scanning Acoustic Microscopy
content: Although additive manufacturing enables the production of metallic components with complex geometries, accurately characterizing their surfaces remains challenging, especially in regions beyond the reach of conventional techniques. To address this challenge, this study investigates scanning acoustic microscopy (SAM) as an automated, non-destructive method for measuring the surface roughness of stainless steel 316L cubes fabricated by selective laser melting. A dedicated image-processing pipeline was developed to detect the water–specimen interface in SAM B-scan images and convert it into a calibrated surface profile. ISO-based spatial filtering was then applied to separate roughness from measurement noise, waviness, and surface form. The resulting profiles were used to calculate Ra, Rq, Rp, Rv, and Rt. Ra was used as the common parameter for quantitative validation of SAM against reference standards. For nominal values of 12.5, 25, and 50 μm, SAM measured 12.92, 28.53, and 51.60 μm, corresponding to absolute deviations of 0.42, 3.53, and 1.60 μm, respectively. The repeatability assessment showed coefficients of variation below 1%, indicating precise measurements. Following this assessment, the proposed pipeline was applied to the fabricated cubes and compared with digital light and laser confocal microscopes. Overall, the findings show that SAM can distinguish different roughness levels and provide reliable quantitative measurements.
